title: Fix 'zsh: permission denied' when running a script on macOS
summary: The Terminal prints 'permission denied' when a script file has no execute permission, which is common for files downloaded from the Internet. These steps check the permission, make the script executable, and run it.

aliases.text: how to make script executable mac
terminal says permission denied for sh file
как сделать скрипт исполняемым на маке

prerequisites: The script file is saved on your Mac, for example in Downloads

steps.explain: Read the message. 'permission denied' on a script means the file has no execute permission, so zsh will not start it as a program. Run the next commands from the folder that holds the script, or use its full path.
Show the permissions of the script. The first column lists them. Look for x letters: they mean the file may be started.

placeholders.name: SCRIPT
placeholders.description: the file name of the script

steps.expect: -rw-r--r-- has no x, so the script is not executable. -rwxr-xr-x has x, so the permission is already set and the error has another cause.

steps.explain: Read the script before you run it, if it came from the Internet. A script can change or delete files on your Mac, so run only scripts you trust.

placeholders.name: SCRIPT
placeholders.description: the file name of the script

steps.expect: The text of the script. It usually starts with a line such as #!/bin/zsh or #!/bin/bash and lists commands one per line.

steps.explain: Add the execute permission to the script for all users. This changes only the permission of this file, not its content.

placeholders.name: SCRIPT
placeholders.description: the file name of the script

alternatives.explain: Add the execute permission for your own user only.

placeholders.name: SCRIPT
placeholders.description: the file name of the script

steps.expect: No output. Run ls -l on the script again to see the x letters in the permissions.

steps.explain: Start the script from the current folder. ./ means 'this folder'.

placeholders.name: SCRIPT
placeholders.description: the file name of the script

alternatives.explain: Run the script with bash without changing its permissions. Use this if the script is written for bash.

placeholders.name: SCRIPT
placeholders.description: the file name of the script

alternatives.expect: The script output appears, the same as with ./.

alternatives.explain: Run the script with zsh without changing its permissions. Use this if the script is written for zsh.

placeholders.name: SCRIPT
placeholders.description: the file name of the script

alternatives.expect: The script output appears, the same as with ./.

steps.expect: The script's own output appears, then the prompt comes back. The 'permission denied' message no longer appears.

verify.expect: The permissions now include x, for example -rwxr-xr-x, and ./<SCRIPT> starts without the 'permission denied' message.

warnings: Run only scripts you trust. Read the file with cat before you run it.
A script can change or delete files on your Mac. Do not run scripts that ask for your administrator password unless you know what they do.
